_comment: 🧩️ This subset's own contribution. `s.remodel.remodel` is a semio-NATIVE artifact carried in `.dsl.semio`/`.pack.semio`, so no third party can serve as its reference — see the noOracleDecision below.

noOracleDecisions.rationale: No third-party crate reads or writes semio's `.dsl.semio`/`.pack.semio` envelope, and no photogrammetry library is authoritative over `RemodelMutation` — this is a reconstruction JOB document, not a point cloud or a mesh file, so a reader of COLMAP, LAS or PLY output would be judging a different artifact. What distinguishes this subset is that its 35 kinds fall into three genuinely different families with different laws: id-keyed create/delete/change over five referential pools (`streams`, `assets`, camera calibrations, rig extrinsics, GCPs — where deleting a stream or a GCP CASCADES into observations that point at it), `update-*-params` over the eight inseparable `ReconstructionParams` sub-records (each replaced whole because its fields are only meaningful together), and `replace-*` over the engine-owned result payloads. Confidence comes from the committed per-kind specification vectors under `../🧬️schema/🧬️mutations/<kind>/🧪️tests/<fixture>/`, already unit-tested inside the production crate, plus the inverse law as a metamorphic property — which for the cascading deletes means the undone document must carry the cascaded observations back, not merely the deleted record. `commit-reconstruction` is the one kind with NO committed vector: its diff reads process-global staging state (`commit_staged_remodel_reconstruction`, `durable_staged_remodel_asset`) that a `(before, mutation, after)` triple cannot carry, so `mutate-remodel-1` exercises it through its own documented refusal path instead and says so in its feature description.
